citations.title: License Requirements
citations.requirement: Facility may not represent any service beyond its license (1). Capacity changes need prior AHCA Central Office approval (2). Converting uninspected space to resident use needs prior Field Office approval (3). Buildings under one license must be on contiguous property (4). Copies of annual fire and sanitation inspections go to AHCA Central Office within 30 calendar days (5). Facility must identify state-funded residents on request (6).

citations.title: Admission Procedures, Appropriateness of Placement and Continued Residency Criteria
citations.requirement: (1) Admission criteria, including age 18+, no stage 3-4 pressure sores, not bedridden except hospice, and the listed nursing services that exclude a resident. (2) Face-to-face medical exam within 60 days before or 30 days after admission, on AHCA Form 1823 or the practitioner's form. (3) Admission package contents, and what the resident receives at or before admission. (4) Continued residency: exam at least every 3 years or after a significant change, bedridden limit of 7 consecutive days, stage 2 sore conditions, and terminally ill/hospice retention.

citations.title: Resident Care Standards
citations.requirement: (1) Supervision and written record of significant changes. (2) Activities program (12 hrs/week, 6 days/week). (3) Arrangement for health care and transportation. (5) Bill of Rights posting, written grievance procedure, posted complaint numbers in 14-point type, house rules, no uncompensated work, telephone access. (6) Third-party services and 30-day communication. (7) Elopement standards. (8) Physical restraint care plan. (9) Assistive devices. (10) Infection control: hand hygiene, standard precautions, equipment disinfection.

citations.title: Medication Practices
citations.requirement: Rules for self-administration, pill organizers, assistance with self-administration by trained unlicensed staff, and administration by licensed staff. Also CLIA certificate when facility staff perform lab tests, medication observation records, storage (locked, central storage triggers), disposal timelines, labeling and orders, and OTC/stock supply.

citations.title: Do Not Resuscitate Orders (DNROs)
citations.requirement: Written DNRO policies. A DNRO may not be required as a condition of admission. At admission, give Form SCHS-4-2006 (or equivalent) and DH Form 1896. Document in the record whether DH Form 1896 is executed. Honor an executed form. Hospice procedures take precedence in an arrest.

citations.title: Staffing Standards
citations.requirement: (1) Administrator qualifications (21+, HS/GED, Level 2 screening, core training and competency test within 90 days), up to 3 facilities, managers appointed in writing, and notice of administrator change within 10 days on AHCA Form 3180-1006. (2) Staff health statement within 30 days, annual TB documentation, Level 2 for staff and contracted staff, written contracts with staffing agencies. (3) Minimum weekly staff-hours table, awake overnight staff at 17+ residents, CPR/First Aid staff at all times, in-charge rules during administrator absence, written 24-hour schedule, AHCA authority to order more staff.

citations.title: Staff Training Requirements and Competency Test
citations.requirement: 26-hr core training plus competency test (75% to pass) within 3 months; 12 hrs CE every 2 years. 2-hr preservice orientation before resident contact. In-service training: infection control, adverse incidents and emergency procedures, resident rights and abuse, behavior and ADLs, safe food handling, elopement, HIV/AIDS. First Aid/CPR. 6-hr medication-assistance course with 2 hrs annual CE. Food service CE. ECC, LMH and ADRD training.

citations.title: Food Service Standards
citations.requirement: Written food service designee. USDA Dietary Guidelines-based menus, reviewed annually by a dietitian or nutritionist. Menus planned 1 week ahead, and menus as served kept 6 months. Therapeutic diets as ordered. Meal-interval limits. 3-day nonperishable food supply. County health department reports kept for 2 years. Contracted food service documentation.

citations.title: Fiscal Standards
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: resident trust funds not co-mingled with facility funds (a single trust account is allowed with separate written accounting per resident) (2). Surety bond if the facility is representative payee or holds power of attorney (3). Liability insurance in force at all times, with proof filed at each renewal or policy change (4).

citations.title: Records
citations.requirement: Records must be readily available at the licensee's physical address. Lists required facility records, including the admission/discharge log, required policies, inspection reports, and the license on display. Also required staff records, resident records, retention (resident contracts 5 years; other resident records 2 years after departure), and inspection access.

citations.title: Resident Contracts
citations.requirement: Contract offered before or at admission with required provisions: services and rates, 30-day written notice of rate increases, deposits and refund policy, written bed hold policy, religious affiliation, transfer notice, 3-year assessment, medication and DNRO policies. Resident gets a copy. Additional charges need an itemized statement and a signed, dated addendum.

citations.title: Emergency Management
citations.requirement: Written CEMP on AHCA Form 3180-5006 (Sept 2023) covering the listed components. Annual submission and county emergency management approval, with significant modifications submitted within 30 days. Staff trained within 30 days of hire. Evacuation reporting within 6 hours. Emergency shelter above licensed capacity with a 48-hour report and a log.

citations.title: Emergency Environmental Control for Assisted Living Facilities
citations.requirement: Plan to hold ambient temperature at or below 81°F for 96 hours after power loss. At least 20 net sq ft per resident, calculated on 80% of licensed beds. Fuel onsite: 48 hrs (16 or fewer beds) or 72 hrs (17+). Carbon monoxide alarm. Plan submitted before licensure. Proof of county approval sent to AHCA within 30 days. Written heat-injury mitigation procedures. Notice to residents within 5 business days.

citations.title: Inspection Responsibilities
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: county health department inspects sanitation, food hygiene and biomedical waste (1). Local fire authority or State Fire Marshal inspects fire safety (2). AHCA inspects everything else (3).

citations.title: Physical Plant Standards
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: Florida Building Code and ch. 69A-40 fire standards (1)-(2). Resident furnishings (3): bed with mattress at least 36x72 inches, closet or wardrobe, dresser, nightstand or table, lamp, wastebasket. Facility keeps master keys, and provides linens and laundry service.

citations.title: Limited Mental Health
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: LMH facility requirements, including a community living support plan and cooperative agreement per mental health resident. Records requirements cross-referenced in 59A-36.015(3)(r). Staffing cross-referenced in 59A-36.010(3)(f).

citations.title: Extended Congregate Care Services
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: ECC license requirements, including a nurse on staff or under contract, monthly nursing assessments, quarterly service plan review, adequate awake staff at all hours, and ECC admission/residency criteria and disclosure.

citations.title: Limited Nursing Services
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: LNS facility must employ or contract a nurse available as needed. Services require a practitioner's order. Monthly nursing assessments and nursing progress notes are kept.

citations.title: Licensing and Change of Ownership
citations.requirement: Licensure application and change-of-ownership procedures (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: License required; fee
citations.requirement: A license is required to operate an ALF (subsec. 1). Specialty licenses ECC and LNS (subsec. 3). Biennial fees (subsec. 4).

citations.title: Limited mental health license
citations.requirement: LMH license requirements and training for facilities serving mental health residents.

citations.title: Contracts
citations.requirement: Resident contract content and refund policy; implemented by Rule 59A-36.018.

citations.title: Appropriateness of placements; examinations of residents
citations.requirement: Medical examination within 60 days before or 30 days after admission (subsec. 5). Hospice exceptions (subsec. 1). Disagreement on placement appropriateness (subsec. 8), as referenced in Rules 59A-36.006 and 59A-36.018.

citations.title: Use of personnel; emergency care
citations.requirement: Facilities with 17 or more beds must keep a working AED on the premises (subsec. 3(a)). The section also underpins the DNRO rule.

citations.title: Property and personal affairs of residents
citations.requirement: Surety bond when acting as representative payee or under a power of attorney (subsec. 2). Safekeeping of up to $500 cash and $500 in personal effects by mutual consent, and verified statements at least every 3 months (subsecs. 3-4), per fact-checked research.

citations.title: Business practice; personnel records; liability insurance
citations.requirement: Records, personnel records and liability insurance (subsec. 3) requirements, per fact-checked research.

citations.title: Resident bill of rights
citations.requirement: Resident Bill of Rights, grievance and facility-procedure rights. It is cited in Rules 59A-36.007(5) and 59A-36.011 and in the fact-checked research. Section text was not independently re-fetched in this pass, so confirm subsection details before quoting them.

citations.title: Staff training and educational requirements
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for core training, 12-hour administrator CE (subsec. 5) and the medication-assistance training (subsec. 6).

citations.title: Background screening
citations.requirement: Level 2 background screening of owners, administrators and staff.

citations.title: Background screening; prohibited offenses
citations.requirement: Level 2 screening standards, with rescreening every 5 years (subsec. 2), per fact-checked research.

citations.title: Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse
citations.requirement: Screening results are shared through the AHCA Clearinghouse (help line 850-412-4503 per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Long-term care managed care plan accountability
citations.requirement: SMMC LTC plans and ALFs negotiate rates. There is no state rate table.

citations.title: Health care licensing application procedures
citations.requirement: Online licensing and renewal filing. Per fact-checked research, renewals must be filed online (effective 3/5/2024).

citations.title: Florida minimum wage
citations.requirement: Minimum wage is $15.00/hr from Sept 30, 2026.

citations.title: Optional State Supplementation
citations.requirement: OSS base provider rate $991.40/month and $160 personal needs allowance (eff. 6/24/2025), per fact-checked research. DCF determines eligibility.

citations.title: Mandatory reporting of abuse, neglect, or exploitation of vulnerable adults
citations.requirement: Statutory duty to report to the Florida Abuse Hotline. NOT fetched and not in the provided research; confirm text before publication.

citations.title: Internal risk management and quality assurance; adverse incidents
citations.requirement: Adverse incident reporting to AHCA and internal risk management. NOT fetched and not in the provided research; confirm timelines before publication.

citations.title: Rules establishing standards (elopement drills)
citations.requirement: Cited in Rule 59A-36.007(7)(c) as the basis for documented elopement drills. Statute text NOT fetched; confirm drill frequency.

citations.title: Assistance with self-administration of medication
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for unlicensed assistance with self-administration (cited in Rules 59A-36.008 and .011). Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Visitation policy
citations.requirement: Cited in Rule 59A-36.015(1)(v) as the basis for the required facility visitation policy. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Notice of change of administrator
citations.requirement: Cited in Rule 59A-36.010(1)(e) (10-day notice). Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Patients with Alzheimer's disease or other related disorders; certain disclosures
citations.requirement: Cited in Rules 59A-36.006(3)(a)13 and 59A-36.015(1)(h) (written description of special Alzheimer's services; keep advertisements). Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Uniform Fire Safety Standards for Assisted Living Facilities
citations.requirement: Fire safety standards enforced by the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal. Referenced in Rules 59A-36.005, .006, .010 and .014. Text NOT fetched. Confirm drill and inspection frequency.

citations.title: Community-based residential facilities (DOH sanitation)
citations.requirement: DOH sanitation and food hygiene standards for ALFs. Referenced in Rules 59A-36.012(3) and 59A-36.015(1)(l). Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Maintenance of records; reports
citations.requirement: Cited in Rule 59A-36.015(1)(m) and (4)(b). AHCA survey, inspection and complaint reports and notices of sanctions are kept 5 years and made available to residents and the public. Statute text NOT fetched.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
state_specifics: The licensee names the administrator. The administrator is responsible for operation and maintenance of the facility, management of all staff, and appropriate care of all residents under Ch. 408 Pt. II, Ch. 429 Pt. I, rule ch. 59A-35 and 59A-36 (59A-36.010(1)).
Owners must notify AHCA Central Office within 10 days of a change of administrator on AHCA Form 3180-1006 (59A-36.010(1)(e)).

An administrator may supervise a maximum of 3 facilities or a single-campus group. A written manager appointment is required for each facility. For up to 3 facilities of 16 or fewer beds each within 15 miles, only 2 managers are required (59A-36.010(1)(c)).
A manager must meet the administrator qualifications and may not manage more than one facility, except as above (59A-36.010(1)(d)).
The administrator monitors continued appropriateness of each resident's placement at all times (59A-36.006(4)(d)).

policies.title: Licensure, Posting and Regulatory Compliance
state_specifics: Display the license in a conspicuous public place (59A-36.015(1)(a)). Do not operate before the license is issued (s. 429.07(1)).
Do not represent any service the facility is not licensed to provide (59A-36.004(1)).
Capacity change or conversion of space to resident use needs prior AHCA approval: Central Office for capacity, Field Office for conversion (59A-36.004(2)-(3)).
Fire safety and sanitation inspections are by the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal and by the county health department. AHCA surveys everything else (59A-36.005).
Send annual fire and sanitation inspection reports to AHCA Central Office within 30 calendar days of each inspection (59A-36.004(5)).

Keep AHCA survey, inspection and complaint reports and notices of sanctions for the last 5 years. Keep fire and sanitation reports for the last 2 years. Make them available to residents and the public (59A-36.015(1)(k)-(m), (4)(b)).
Renewals are filed online (59A-35.060; research states effective 3/5/2024). Licenses are biennial. AHCA recommends filing at least 60 days early to avoid a late fee.
Specialty licenses: ECC, LNS, LMH. Track which licenses the facility holds, and keep admission and services within that scope (59A-36.006(1)(a)15.c).
AHCA Assisted Living Unit contact: (850) 412-4304, assistedliving@ahca.myflorida.com.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Rule 59A-36.015(1) requires these written policies to be on file and readily available at the licensee's address: grievance procedure; elopement response; policies under 59A-36.007(10) (infection control); abuse prevention; medication practices; physical restraints; assistive devices; third-party providers; visitation; DNRO (59A-36.009); and the emergency power policies (59A-36.025(5)).
Records may be electronic, but staff must be able to produce them immediately on request (59A-36.015 preamble; 59A-36.025(5)(b)).
Emergency power policies must also be available for inspection by residents, their representatives and estates (59A-36.025(5)(c)).
Set a defined annual review cycle (operator choice). The CEMP review is mandated annually by 59A-36.019(2).

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: Operator-level program. No standard-license rule in the fetched chapter prescribes a QAPI committee. Tie it to administrator responsibility under 59A-36.010(1).

Inputs to review: grievances and resident suggestions (59A-36.007(5)(b)), adverse incident reports, elopement drills, medication errors recorded on the medication observation record (59A-36.008(5)(b)4), and AHCA survey findings.
Document any AHCA-ordered corrective action plan for increased staffing and its modification or closure (59A-36.010(3)(d)1-2).
VERIFY s. 429.23 (internal risk management/QA) before citing as a mandate. It was not fetched.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Medicaid assisted living is paid through SMMC Long-Term Care plans. The facility and each plan negotiate rates, and there is no state rate table (s. 409.982).
OSS residents: facility receives the OSS base provider rate ($991.40/month, eff. 6/24/2025) and the resident keeps a $160 personal needs allowance (Rule 65A-2.036). DCF determines eligibility.
Keep the OSS Alternate Care Certification form CF-ES 1006 in the record of each OSS resident. Absence is not a basis for action if a good-faith effort to obtain it is documented (59A-36.015(3)(l)).
Identify state-funded residents to AHCA and DCF on request (59A-36.004(6)).
Charges for items covered in the contract rate are prohibited (59A-36.018(3)).

policies.title: Fiscal Standards, Liability Insurance and Surety Bond
state_specifics: Keep resident funds separate from facility funds. One trust account is permitted if a separate written accounting is kept for each resident (59A-36.013(2)).

Liability insurance must be in force at all times. Per fact-checked research, the certificate shows facility name, street address, ALF type, licensed capacity and coverage dates. File proof with AHCA at each renewal or policy change (59A-36.013(4); s. 429.275(3)). No dollar minimum appears in the rule.

Surety bond if the facility is representative payee or holds power of attorney: equal to twice the average monthly aggregate resident income received, or per resident under a POA (s. 429.27(2); 59A-36.013(3), per research). Keep a copy of the bond in effect on file (59A-36.015(1)(f)). Keep the current policy on file (59A-36.015(1)(e)).
Workers' compensation is required with 4 or more employees (s. 440.02(17)(b)2, per research).

policies.title: Resident Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: Post the Resident Bill of Rights (s. 429.28) or the Ombudsman summary in full view in a freely accessible resident area, and include it in the admission package (59A-36.007(5)(a)).

Written house rules in the admission package must address at least: resident responsibilities; alcohol and tobacco use; medication storage; elopement; reporting abuse, neglect and exploitation; administrative and housekeeping schedules; infection control and standard precautions; third-party providers; assistive devices; and physical restraints (59A-36.007(5)(d)).

Residents may not be required to work without compensation. They may be required to clean their own sleeping areas only if the rules or contract say so. A resident-employee must be paid under state and federal wage law (59A-36.007(5)(e)).

Residents have convenient access to a telephone, and unidentified calls must be allowed. At 17+ capacity without private phones, a readily accessible phone is required on each floor of each resident building (59A-36.007(5)(f)).
A facility may not require residents to use a particular health care provider (59A-36.007(3)(c)).
Federal HCBS settings rule applies only to residents funded through Medicaid HCBS waiver or LTC plans.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: A written grievance procedure for receiving and responding to resident complaints, and a written procedure for residents to recommend policy changes, are required. The facility must be able to show that it was applied on receipt of a complaint (59A-36.007(5)(b); 59A-36.015(1)(i)).

Post complaint numbers in full view of a common area near a resident-accessible telephone, in at least 14-point type: Long-Term Care Ombudsman 1-888-831-0404; Disability Rights Florida 1-800-342-0823; AHCA Consumer Hotline 1-888-419-3456; Florida Abuse Hotline 1-800-962-2873 (1-800-96-ABUSE) (59A-36.007(5)(c)).
Show resident participation in activity planning through resident meetings, a council, a suggestion box or similar (59A-36.007(2)(b)).

policies.title: Ombudsman Access
state_specifics: Give each resident or representative a Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program brochure showing the district office telephone number and address before or at admission (59A-36.006(3)(b)4).
Post the Ombudsman number 1-888-831-0404 with the other complaint numbers (59A-36.007(5)(c)).
Display the Ombudsman summary of rights as an acceptable substitute for the full Bill of Rights posting (59A-36.007(5)(a)).
Surveyor and ombudsman access to residents and records is governed by 59A-36.015(4) and s. 429.35 (statute text not fetched).

policies.title: Admission Agreement, Fees, Deposits and Refunds
state_specifics: The contract must be offered for execution by the resident or legal representative before or at admission. Give the resident a copy (59A-36.018(1)-(2)).

Required provisions: services, supplies and accommodations; daily, weekly or monthly rate; additional services and charges or an attached fee schedule; at least 30 days' written notice before any rate increase; purpose of advance or deposit payments and refund policy conforming to s. 429.24(3); written bed hold policy; religious affiliation; written notice of need to transfer if needs exceed the license; assessment on admission and every 3 years; medication and OTC policies; and DNRO policy (59A-36.018(1)(a)-(m)).

Bed hold: the contracted rate may be charged until written notice of a change in status is received, unless the resident's medical condition prevents notice and there is no responsible party (59A-36.018(1)(h)).
Additional charges need an advance itemized written statement and a signed, dated addendum (59A-36.018(3)).
The admission package, less the contract, is kept on file (59A-36.015(1)(g)). Contracts are kept 5 years (59A-36.015(3)(q)).

policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property
state_specifics: Safekeeping of up to $500 cash and $500 in personal effects by mutual consent. Give each resident a verified statement at least every 3 months (s. 429.27(3)-(4), per research).

Facilities acting under power of attorney: keep a copy of the monthly written statement of every transaction made for the resident. Facilities with a separate trust fund: keep a copy of the quarterly statement of funds and property disbursed (59A-36.015(3)(j)-(k)).
Surety bond is required if the facility is representative payee or holds power of attorney (s. 429.27(2); 59A-36.013(3)).
Do not co-mingle resident and facility funds (59A-36.013(2)).

policies.title: Advance Directives and Do Not Resuscitate Orders
federal: 42 CFR 489.102 (not applicable to ALFs; do not cite)
state_specifics: Give each resident or representative at admission Form SCHS-4-2006 "Health Care Advance Directives - The Patient's Right to Decide" (or a substantially similar ch. 765 document) and DH Form 1896 (59A-36.009(1)(a)).
Never require execution or waiver of DH Form 1896 as a condition of admission or treatment. Doing so exposes the license to revocation under s. 408.815 (59A-36.009(1)(a), (2)).
Document in each record whether a DH Form 1896 has been executed. If one has, keep the yellow copy. If a copy was not received, document that it was requested (59A-36.009(1)(b)).
The executed form must be readily available to medical staff in an emergency (59A-36.009(1)(c)).

Staff trained in CPR or a health care provider present may withhold CPR when a valid DH Form 1896 is in place. For hospice residents, call hospice immediately and hospice procedures take precedence (59A-36.009(3)).
The facility's DNRO and advance directive policy is part of the admission package (59A-36.006(3)(a)11).
Keep documentation of any health care surrogate, proxy, guardian or power of attorney in the record (59A-36.015(3)(m)).

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Resident records must be available to the resident, the legal representative, designee, surrogate, guardian, attorney in fact or case manager, the resident's estate, and others authorized in writing or by law (59A-36.015(4)(a)).
Residents are entitled to a copy of their records on departure (59A-36.015(3)(q)).
Residents have the right to private communication, including telephone use (59A-36.007(5)(f)).

Apply HIPAA 45 CFR 160/164 only if the facility is a covered entity (e.g., it bills electronically for health care services). Otherwise, apply this policy as operator best practice. The facility must decide and document its status.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
federal: Title VI, 42 U.S.C. 2000d (if the facility receives federal financial assistance)
state_specifics: An individual with HIV infection may be admitted if otherwise eligible (59A-36.006(1)(a)2).

Required admission documents must be in English. If the resident cannot read or understand English and translated documents are not available, the facility must explain its policies to a family member, friend or other individual who can communicate them to the resident (59A-36.006(3)(c)).
Admission decisions rest on the 59A-36.006(1) criteria and the individual assessment of strengths, needs and preferences, not on any other basis (59A-36.006(1)(a)15).

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening and Admission Criteria
state_specifics: Admission criteria (standard, LNS or LMH license): 18+; free of communicable disease likely to be transmitted; able to perform ADLs with supervision or assistance; able to transfer (more than one person's help permitted); able to take medication by self-administration, assistance or administration; dietary needs the facility can meet; not a danger to self or others; no 24-hour licensed mental health treatment; not bedridden (except hospice); no stage 3 or 4 pressure sores; no 24-hour nursing supervision; no skilled rehabilitative services (59A-36.006(1)(a)).

Excluded nursing services for standard, LNS and LMH: artificial airway (CPAP/BiPAP permitted), tube feeding assistance, blood gas monitoring, post-surgical drains or wound vacuums, blood products, and unstabilized surgical wounds. Standard and LMH-only facilities also exclude dialysis and IV therapy performed in the facility (59A-36.006(1)(a)11-12).

The administrator decides appropriateness based on assessment of strengths, needs and preferences, the medical exam, the admission policy and services offered, and the ability to meet ch. 69A-40 fire standards (59A-36.006(1)(a)15).

Medical exam: face-to-face by a health care practitioner within 60 days before or 30 days after admission, on AHCA Form 1823 (April 2021) or the practitioner's form. Missing items must be obtained and documented within 30 days of admission (59A-36.006(2)).
CARES assessments may substitute for the exam. DCF- or agency-placed residents must be examined within 30 days before placement (59A-36.006(2)(c)-(d)).
Temporary emergency DCF placements are exempt from the exam for up to 30 days. They must be logged and counted in the census, and may not push the facility over licensed capacity (59A-36.006(2)(f)).

Before admission, make available the written admission package (criteria, rates, services, house rules, DNRO/advance directive policy, ECC criteria if applicable, ADRD description if advertised, elopement policies). At or before admission, give the contract, the package, the Bill of Rights and the Ombudsman brochure (59A-36.006(3)).
Unlicensed assistance with medication requires written informed consent from the resident or surrogate, and the resident must be told the staff's professional qualifications (59A-36.006(1)(a)5.a).

policies.title: Resident Assessment and Reassessment
state_specifics: Health assessment on admission, then face-to-face by a health care practitioner at least every 3 years or after a significant change, whichever comes first (59A-36.006(4); 59A-36.018(1)(k)). "Significant change" is defined in 59A-36.002, which was not fetched; copy its definition into the manual after verifying.

Every resident must be assessed for elopement risk by a health care provider or mental health provider within 30 calendar days of admission. A pre-admission health assessment satisfies this (59A-36.007(7)(a)).
Contact the health care provider and appropriate family, guardian, surrogate or case manager if the resident exhibits a significant change (59A-36.007(1)(d)).
ECC and LNS: monthly nursing assessments (per research; see 59A-36.021 and .022).
A resident whose needs exceed the license must receive written notice to arrange a transfer (59A-36.018(1)(j)).

policies.title: Resident Care Record, Significant Change Documentation and Service Planning
state_specifics: Standard ALF rules do not require a comprehensive written care plan. They require a written record, updated as needed, of significant changes, illnesses resulting in medical attention, changes in the method of medication administration, and other changes that resulted in additional services (59A-36.007(1)(f); 59A-36.015(3)(e)).
Residents for whom a physician has prescribed a physical restraint need a written care plan within 14 days of prescribing and before use (59A-36.007(8)).

ECC: quarterly service plan review (per research; 59A-36.021). LMH: community living support plan and cooperative agreement for each mental health resident (per research; 59A-36.020). Hospice: interdisciplinary care plan from hospice in consultation with the facility (59A-36.006(4)(c)3).
Stage 3-4 pressure sores are excluded. A stage 2 sore is allowed only on the 59A-36.006 conditions (see ADM-04 and HCS-07).

Resident weight: record at admission and semi-annually for residents receiving ADL assistance, unless hospice residents or their representatives or physicians request in writing that weights not be taken (59A-36.015(3)(f)).

policies.title: Continued Residency Criteria and Conditions the Facility Cannot Serve
state_specifics: Continued residency criteria equal admission criteria except for the exceptions in 59A-36.006(4)(a)-(c).
A resident may be bedridden for no more than 7 consecutive days unless receiving licensed hospice services (59A-36.006(4)(a)).

Stage 2 pressure sore: may stay if the resident contracts directly with a licensed home health agency or nurse, or the facility has an LNS license and care follows a practitioner's plan of care. The condition must be documented in the record. If no improvement within 30 days as documented by a health care practitioner, discharge is required (59A-36.006(4)(b)).

Terminally ill resident who no longer meets criteria may stay if: hospice admits the resident and the resident consents; resident (or representative) and facility agree; hospice and the facility develop an interdisciplinary care plan; documentation is in the file (59A-36.006(4)(c)).
A hospice resident may receive only services within the scope of the facility's license from facility staff (59A-36.006(4)(e)).
Nursing staff may not train or delegate the excluded skilled nursing tasks to unlicensed persons (59A-36.006(1)(c)).

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Relocation Notice
state_specifics: When the administrator or health care provider decides the resident needs services beyond the license, notify the resident, representative or acting agency in writing that the resident must arrange transfer. If the resident has no representative, refer the resident to the social service agency. If the parties disagree on appropriateness, s. 429.26(8) applies (59A-36.018(1)(j)).
Notify family, guardian, health care surrogate or case manager when a resident is discharged or moves out (59A-36.007(1)(e)).

Admission/discharge log: record date of discharge, reason, and the facility or home address of discharge. Readmission needs a new entry. A discharge is not required when a bed is held (59A-36.015(1)(b)).

On departure, return all medications to the resident, family or guardian. After notice and a 15-day wait, remaining medications are abandoned and must be disposed of within 30 days with documentation (59A-36.008(6)(e)-(f)).
Residents get a copy of their records on departure (59A-36.015(3)(q)).
VERIFY the statutory notice period for involuntary relocation in s. 429.28 (not re-fetched) before stating a number of days in this policy.

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage and Disposal
state_specifics: Residents who can self-administer must be encouraged and allowed to (59A-36.008(1)(a)). Residents may keep medications on or off premises, and may store them in their rooms if the room is locked when they are absent or the medication is out of sight in a secure place (59A-36.008(6)(a)).

Central storage is mandatory if the facility administers medications, the resident requests it, the provider documents the medication as hazardous, the resident cannot keep it safe, other residents are at risk, or facility rules require it (59A-36.008(6)(b)).

Centrally stored medications: locked at all times, free of dampness and abnormal temperature, refrigerated items kept locked (container, refrigerator or room), keys or codes always accessible to responsible staff, kept separate from other residents' medications (59A-36.008(6)(c)).
Discontinued but unexpired medication: return to the resident, or store separately in an area marked "discontinued medication" (59A-36.008(6)(d)).

Abandoned or expired medication: dispose within 30 days of the determination. Document in the resident record. Pharmacist disposal or destruction by the administrator or designee with one witness (59A-36.008(6)(f)).

Labeling: only a pharmacist may transfer medication between containers (pill organizers excepted). "As needed" or "as directed" orders need clarification from the provider. Changes in directions need a signed order. Telephone orders by a nurse need a written order within 10 working days (59A-36.008(7)).
OTC stock supply: locked, labeled with the name, purchase date and a notice that it is stock supply. Record each dose in the resident's medication observation record (59A-36.008(8)(a)).
Sample medications must stay in the manufacturer's packaging or a container with a label naming the practitioner, resident, date, drug, strength, directions and expiration date (59A-36.008(7)(g)).

A facility that performs lab tests such as blood glucose must hold a CLIA certificate. Not required if residents test themselves or staff assist using the residents' equipment (59A-36.008(4)(d)). AHCA Laboratory Unit: (850) 412-4500.

policies.title: Medication Administration and Staff Authorization
state_specifics: Unlicensed staff providing assistance with self-administration must be 18+ and complete the training in 59A-36.011(6) before assuming that duty (59A-36.008(3)(a)).

Assistance means orally advising the resident of the medication name and dosage and verbally prompting the resident. Staff must observe the resident take the medication. Concerns or suspected noncompliance go to the provider and are documented (59A-36.008(3)(b), (d)).
"Judgment" and "discretion" mean interpreting vital signs and evaluating or assessing a resident's condition. Unlicensed staff may not perform those tasks (59A-36.008(3)(g)).
Unlicensed staff may not manage pill organizers. Only a nurse may fill them, and only for residents who self-administer (59A-36.008(2)).

Administration requires a licensed staff member available to administer per the provider's order or label (59A-36.008(4)(a)). Unusual reactions or significant changes must be documented and reported immediately to the provider (59A-36.008(4)(b)).
Training: 6-hr course taught by a RN or licensed pharmacist who issues a certificate after in-person demonstration, then 2 hrs of annual CE, which may be online (59A-36.011(6)(b)-(c)).

Daily medication observation record for each resident receiving assistance or administration. Updated at each dose, showing name, allergies, provider and telephone number, drug, strength, directions, and any missed dose, refusal or error (59A-36.008(5)(b)).
Medications that serve as chemical restraints: keep a record of the prescribing physician's annual evaluation (59A-36.008(5)(c)).
The facility must tell residents the professional qualifications of staff providing assistance. Obtain written informed consent when unlicensed staff assist (59A-36.006(1)(a)5.a).

policies.title: Nursing Services, LNS License and Limits on Delegation
state_specifics: Standard-license nursing: a nurse on staff or under contract is needed to (a) provide assistance with portable oxygen and routine colostomy care of stoma site flange placement or train the resident to do it, and (b) administer medications (59A-36.006(1)(a)5.b, (1)(b)).

Nursing staff may not train unlicensed persons to perform skilled nursing services or delegate the excluded tasks to CNAs or unlicensed persons (59A-36.006(1)(c)). Residents may contract independently with a licensed third party if the facility agrees.

LNS license (s. 429.07(3)(c); Rule 59A-36.022, per research): employ or contract a nurse available as needed. Services need a practitioner's order. Keep monthly nursing assessments and nursing progress notes.
A nurse may take a telephone medication order, which must be documented promptly, with a written order obtained within 10 working days (59A-36.008(7)(e)).
A nurse counts as having completed First Aid training (59A-36.010(3)(a)5.b).
Staff providing services that require licensure must be appropriately licensed or certified, and copies kept in the personnel file (59A-36.010(2)(b); 59A-36.015(2)(a)2).

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: Contact the resident's health care provider and the family, guardian, health care surrogate or case manager when a resident exhibits a significant change (59A-36.007(1)(d)).
Document significant changes, illnesses resulting in medical attention, medication administration changes and added services in the resident record (59A-36.007(1)(f)).
Report to the provider health changes that could be due to medications, and any unusual reactions. Document each contact in the record (59A-36.008(1)(b), (4)(b)).
All staff observe residents, document observations in the resident's record and report to the provider as appropriate to their qualifications (59A-36.010(2)(b)).

Hospital or other transfers: bed hold must be addressed in the contract. Charges continue until written notice of a change in status unless the resident cannot give notice and has no representative (59A-36.018(1)(h)).
Emergency: executed DH Form 1896 must be readily available to medical staff (59A-36.009(1)(c)). Hospice residents: call hospice first (59A-36.009(3)(b)).
Send the medication list and DNRO status with the resident (best practice).

policies.title: Dementia and Memory Care
state_specifics: A facility that advertises special care for Alzheimer's disease and related disorders (ADRD) or maintains secured areas under Florida Building Code Ch. 4 s. 464.4.6 must ensure that staff receive ADRD training under 59A-36.011(10). The research ties this to s. 430.5025. Confirm the training hours against the full text of 59A-36.011(10), which was truncated in the fetch.
Keep copies of all ADRD advertisements (59A-36.015(1)(h)). Give prospective residents the written description of special services required by s. 429.177 (59A-36.006(3)(a)13).
Identify residents with ADRD and mobility limitations in the CEMP for specialized assistance (59A-36.019(1)(e)).
Residents at risk for elopement need identification on their person (name, facility name, address and phone, checked at least daily) and a photo ID on file (59A-36.007(7)(a)1-2).
A resident who requires 24-hour licensed mental health treatment or poses a danger to self or others is outside admission criteria (59A-36.006(1)(a)7-8).

policies.title: Falls Prevention
state_specifics: Operator policy. The ALF rule has no standalone falls standard. Anchor it to supervision and daily observation of each resident's health, safety and well-being (59A-36.007(1)(b)) and to written documentation of illnesses or changes that result in medical attention (59A-36.007(1)(f)).
Include assistive device safety checks (see HCS-10).
Include medication side-effect review: report observable health changes to the provider (59A-36.008(1)(b)).
Staff must provide enough supervision for residents' scheduled and unscheduled needs (59A-36.010(3)(b)).
A fall that causes injury should also be reviewed under SAF-02 as an incident. Confirm with s. 429.23 (not fetched) whether it is a reportable adverse incident.

policies.title: Skin Integrity
state_specifics: Stage 3 or 4 pressure sores bar admission (59A-36.006(1)(a)10).

A stage 2 sore is allowed only if: the resident contracts directly with a licensed home health agency or a nurse, or (in an LNS facility) the facility cares for the resident under a practitioner's plan of care; the condition is documented in the record and the admission and discharge logs; and discharge follows if there is no improvement within 30 days as documented by a health care practitioner (59A-36.006(1)(a)10, (4)(b)).
Note the stage 2 sore on the admission log entry (59A-36.015(1)(b)1).
Treatment of surgical incisions or wounds is allowed only if the wound and underlying condition are stabilized and a plan of care is in the record (59A-36.006(1)(a)11.f).
A bedridden resident may remain for no more than 7 consecutive days unless in hospice (59A-36.006(4)(a)).

policies.title: Hospice, Home Health and Third-Party Provider Coordination
state_specifics: A resident enrolled in licensed hospice may be admitted and may remain under 59A-36.006(1)(d) and (4)(c). Hospice resident documentation includes the interdisciplinary care plan (59A-36.015(3)(n)).
Hospice residents may be bedridden and may need 24-hour nursing under s. 429.26(1)(c) (59A-36.006(1)(a)9, 13).
Hospice procedures take precedence when a hospice resident has a cardiac or pulmonary arrest. Staff must immediately contact hospice (59A-36.009(3)(b)).

Third-party services (home health, private nurse, outpatient clinic) must be allowed if the resident meets admission and continued residency criteria. The facility policy must require the third party to coordinate with the facility on the resident's condition and services (59A-36.007(6)(a)-(b)).

Documented communication with each third-party provider at least every 30 days and at any significant change. If treatment is less frequent than monthly, follow the treatment schedule. If contact fails, document two attempts on separate days with the name, method, date and time (59A-36.007(6)(c)).
If the facility assists in arranging third-party services, document why efforts were unsuccessful or declined (59A-36.007(6)(d)).
Keep the facility's policy on third-party providers on file (59A-36.015(1)(u)).

policies.title: Death of a Resident
state_specifics: Record the date of death on the admission and discharge log (59A-36.015(1)(b)2).
Notify the resident's representative or family (and hospice, if applicable) per the resident's documented contacts (59A-36.015(3)(a)8).
For a resident with an executed DH Form 1896, follow 59A-36.009. For a hospice resident, hospice procedures take precedence (59A-36.009(3)).
Return the resident's medications to the family or guardian. Abandoned or expired medications are disposed of within 30 days with documentation (59A-36.008(6)(e)-(f)).
Keep resident records for 2 years after departure, and contracts for 5 years (59A-36.015(3)(q)).
Any reporting of a death for adverse-incident purposes depends on s. 429.23, which was not fetched; confirm before adding reporting deadlines.

policies.title: Assistive Devices Safety
state_specifics: The facility is responsible for the safe use of residents' assistive devices (59A-36.007(9)).

Written policies must set requirements and methods for assessing the physical condition of devices that may injure a resident and for recommending repair or replacement (59A-36.007(9)(a)). This policy must be kept on file (59A-36.015(1)(t)).
Document each resident's assistive devices in the resident record (59A-36.007(9)(b)).

Direct care staff using assistive devices must know how to operate them (59A-36.007(9)(c)). Devices must be clean, in good repair and free of hazards (59A-36.007(9)(d)). Encourage independence in device use (59A-36.007(9)(e)).
Communal devices and reusable medical equipment must be cleaned and disinfected before and after each use per manufacturer's recommendations (59A-36.007(10)(c)).

policies.title: Extended Congregate Care (ECC) Program
state_specifics: Applies only if the facility holds an ECC license. Delete otherwise.

The ECC license may be provisional for no more than 6 months for facilities licensed under 2 years, followed by an unannounced inspection (s. 429.07(3)(b); per research). The administrator needs 2 years of qualifying experience (a bachelor's degree can substitute for 1 year) per research.
Nurse on staff or under contract. Monthly nursing assessments. Quarterly service plan review. Adequate awake staff at all hours (per research; 59A-36.021).

Training: administrator and ECC supervisor complete core training plus 4 hours of initial ECC training before ECC licensure (or within 3 months of employment in a licensed ECC facility), then 4 hours of CE every 2 years. Direct care staff complete 2 hours of ECC in-service within 6 months of hire (59A-36.011(8)).
Provide prospective residents the ECC residency criteria, description of added services with costs, and any limits on where ECC residents may live (59A-36.006(3)(a)12).
ECC licensees must also meet the staffing rules of 59A-36.021 (59A-36.010(3)(f)). Records per 59A-36.015(1)(w).

policies.title: Limited Mental Health (LMH) Program
state_specifics: Applies only if the facility holds an LMH license. Delete otherwise. Per research, an LMH license is needed before admitting any mental health resident.

Training: administrator, managers and staff with direct contact with mental health residents must have 6 hours of specialized training provided or approved by DCF within 6 months of licensure or of employment, then 3 hours of CE every 2 years (59A-36.011(9)(a)).
The initial 6 hours count once toward 6 of the 12 hours of administrator/manager CE, and the 3 hours of CE count toward the 12-hour requirement (59A-36.011(9)(a)1.b, 3).

CE topics: mental health diagnoses; mental health needs, services and behaviors; resident progress in treatment; recognizing changes in condition; crisis services and Baker Act procedures (59A-36.011(9)(a)2).
Training certificates travel with staff between employers. Keep a copy in the personnel file (59A-36.011(9)(b)).
Keep each resident's community living support plan and cooperative agreement (per research; 59A-36.020). No extra AHCA fee (per research).

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Post the Florida Abuse Hotline number 1-800-962-2873 (1-800-96-ABUSE) near a resident-accessible telephone, in at least 14-point type (59A-36.007(5)(c)).

Training: direct care staff who have not taken core training get 1 hour within 30 days of hire on resident rights and on recognizing and reporting abuse, neglect and exploitation, using the facility's abuse prevention policies and procedures (59A-36.011(3)(c)).
Keep the written abuse prevention policies and procedures on file (59A-36.015(1)(q)). House rules must address reporting of abuse, neglect and exploitation (59A-36.007(5)(d)5).
Level 2 screening of staff and contracted staff before they work with residents (59A-36.010(2)(f)).
Mandatory reporting to the Abuse Hotline is under ch. 415 (s. 415.1034). It was not fetched. Verify who must report and the immediacy wording before publication.

Residents may not be required to work without compensation (59A-36.007(5)(e)). Staff may not serve as attorney in fact without the required monthly statement and surety bond (59A-36.015(3)(j); s. 429.27).

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
state_specifics: Direct care staff must receive 1 hour of in-service training within 30 days of hire on reporting adverse incidents and on facility emergency procedures, including chain of command and staff roles in evacuation (59A-36.011(3)(b)).
Document significant changes and illnesses resulting in medical attention in the resident record (59A-36.007(1)(f)).
Report medication errors, refusals and missed doses on the medication observation record (59A-36.008(5)(b)4).

Adverse incident reporting to AHCA and risk management duties arise under s. 429.23, which was not fetched or in the research. Verify definitions, report forms and time limits before publishing them in this policy.
Notify the county emergency management agency and AHCA of evacuations within 6 hours of the order (59A-36.019(4)(a)).

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Written elopement response policies and procedures must provide for: an immediate search of the facility and premises; identified staff and their duties; staff responsible for contacting law enforcement, family, guardian, health care surrogate and case manager if the resident is not found; and continued care of the other residents (59A-36.007(7)(b)).

Residents assessed at risk or with any history of elopement must be identified to staff. All residents are assessed for risk within 30 days of admission. Daily effort to check at-risk residents carry ID with their name and the facility's name, address and phone. Photo ID on file, accessible to staff and law enforcement (59A-36.007(7)(a)).

Conduct and document elopement drills under s. 429.41(1)(k) (59A-36.007(7)(c)). Frequency is set by statute and was not fetched, so confirm it. Keep documented drills on file (59A-36.015(1)(o)). Keep documentation of direct care staff and administrator participation in the personnel file (59A-36.015(2)(a)5).
Training: all staff within 30 days of employment, each given a copy of the policy and each showing competency (59A-36.011(3)(f)).
Include the elopement policy in the admission package and the house rules (59A-36.006(3)(a)14; 59A-36.007(5)(d)4).

policies.title: Physical and Chemical Restraints and Restrictive Practices
state_specifics: Physical restraints require a physician's prescription. A written care plan is needed within 14 days of prescribing and before use. It specifies the device, the maximum daily time applied, and how and how often staff will monitor and report to the physician any injury, agitation, depression or decline in mobility (59A-36.007(8)).
The physician reviews continued appropriateness at least annually. Keep the review in the record (59A-36.007(8)(c)).
If a resident's ability to remove or avoid a device fluctuates, treat it as a physical restraint (59A-36.007(8)(c)).
Staff must apply the device appropriately and safely (59A-36.007(8)(b)).
Medications that serve as chemical restraints require a record of the prescribing physician's annual evaluation (59A-36.008(5)(c)).
Keep the facility's physical restraint policy on file and cover it in the house rules (59A-36.015(1)(s); 59A-36.007(5)(d)10).
Secured units: see HCS-05.

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Disaster Plan
state_specifics: Written CEMP on AHCA Form 3180-5006, "Minimum Emergency Management Planning Criteria for Assisted Living Facilities" (Sept 2023). Cover all hazards; care of residents who stay; care and transfer of residents evacuated (records, transportation, sheltering, supplies, staffing, equipment, medications); care of evacuees received; residents with ADRD or mobility limits; county coordination; post-disaster activities including family inquiries and reporting relocations to the county; and staff responsible for each part (59A-36.019(1)).

Review and submit the plan annually to the county emergency management agency (s. 408.821(1) as cited in 59A-36.019(2)(a)). The county is the final authority (59A-36.019(2)(b)). A significant modification must be submitted within 30 days (59A-36.019(2)(a)1).

Train all staff on their duties. New staff must be trained on the plan within 30 days of employment (59A-36.019(3)(a)). If telephones fail, request help from law enforcement or emergency management (59A-36.019(3)(b)).

Evacuate if directed by the county. Report the evacuation to the county and AHCA within 6 hours of the order. Do not re-occupy until the county clears reentry and the facility can meet residents' needs. Keep a 24/7 contact person for AHCA. Know the location of all residents until relocated (59A-36.019(4)).

Emergency shelter above licensed capacity is allowed during a declared state of emergency if life safety is not jeopardized and needs can be met. Report the overage to the AHCA Field Office within 48 hours, or to Central Office at (850) 412-4304, and keep a log with name, usual address and arrival and departure dates (59A-36.019(5)).
Keep a 3-day supply of nonperishable food and water, or a water plan reviewed by local disaster preparedness authority (59A-36.012(2)(h)).
Keep the approved plan with documentation of county approval, readily available (59A-36.015(1)(d)).

policies.title: Emergency Environmental Control (96-Hour Alternate Power)
state_specifics: Detailed plan supplementing the CEMP for loss of primary power. Hold ambient temperature at or below 81°F for at least 96 hours in the designated area(s) (59A-36.025(1)(a)).
Plan at least 20 net square feet per resident, using 80% of licensed bed capacity (59A-36.025(1)(a)1).

Fuel onsite: 48 hours for licensed capacity of 16 or fewer beds; 72 hours for 17 or more. In a declared state of emergency that may affect power, secure 96 hours (portable containers allowed for the rest). Piped natural gas qualifies. If local rules limit fuel storage, plan for the maximum onsite and a reliable method of obtaining more at least 24 hours before depletion (59A-36.025(1)(b)).
Contract for maintenance and testing of the equipment (59A-36.025(1)(c)). Have and maintain a carbon monoxide alarm (59A-36.025(1)(d)).

A new facility submits the plan before licensure and implements it before the license is issued (59A-36.025(2)(a), (4)(b)). Within 30 days of county approval, email proof of approval to assistedliving@ahca.myflorida.com, along with a consumer-friendly summary (59A-36.025(3)(b)-(c)).

Notify each resident and legal representative in writing within 5 business days of initial submission and of final implementation. Annual submissions need no notice unless there is a significant modification (59A-36.025(8)).

Written policies and procedures for heat-injury mitigation must cover cooling devices, ice and refrigeration for medications, staff wellness checks for dehydration and heat injury, and medical intervention for residents in jeopardy (59A-36.025(5)(a)).

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
state_specifics: The local fire authority or State Fire Marshal inspects under ch. 69A-40 (59A-36.005(2)). Send each annual report to AHCA within 30 days (59A-36.004(5)). Keep reports for 2 years (59A-36.015(1)(k)).
AHCA may require additional staff if the local fire authority reports that the facility fails fire safety standards, until the authority confirms compliance (59A-36.010(3)(d)).
Admission decisions must consider the facility's ability to meet ch. 69A-40 for the resident (59A-36.006(1)(a)15.d).
Staff are trained within 30 days of hire in facility emergency procedures including chain of command and evacuation roles (59A-36.011(3)(b)).
Ch. 69A-40 drill frequency, alarm and sprinkler requirements were not fetched. Verify them and add them to this policy.
Physical plant: Florida Building Code and ch. 69A-40 compliance (59A-36.014(1)-(2), per research).

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Hand hygiene program before and after personal services when exposure to infectious materials or body fluids is expected. Alcohol rub, antiseptic wash or soap and water (59A-36.007(10)(a)).
Standard precautions, with gloves, gown, mask, eye protection or face shield depending on the exposure (59A-36.007(10)(b)).
Clean and disinfect reusable medical equipment and communal assistive devices before and after each use per manufacturer's recommendations (59A-36.007(10)(c)).

Training: 1 hour of infection control, including universal precautions and facility sanitation, before providing personal care (except nurses, CNAs and home health aides). Use the facility's infection control policies. A 29 CFR 1910.1030 bloodborne pathogens training record satisfies the requirement (59A-36.011(3)(a)).
Admission screening excludes residents with communicable disease likely to be transmitted. The medical exam must address TB, MRSA, scabies and other communicable disease (59A-36.006(1)(a)2, (2)(a)6).
Staff with a known or suspected communicable disease are removed from duty until a provider's statement shows no risk (59A-36.010(2)(a)2).

Trained staff must follow infection control procedures when assisting with medications (59A-36.008(3)(h)). Biomedical waste and sanitation inspections are by the county health department (59A-36.005(1)).

policies.title: Smoking, Alcohol, Visitors and Pets
state_specifics: House rules in the admission package must cover alcohol and tobacco use (59A-36.007(5)(d)2).

A written visitation policy under s. 408.823(2)(a) is a required facility record (59A-36.015(1)(v)). Per research, the visitation policy is also an AHCA application attachment on initial and renewal applications.
Resident privacy and telephone access rights must be respected (59A-36.007(5)(f)).
Pet policy is an operator choice. If service animals are allowed, address them with ADA obligations and infection control (59A-36.007(10)).
Smoking restrictions beyond house rules: confirm Florida Clean Indoor Air Act (Ch. 386, Pt. II) requirements. These were not fetched.

policies.title: CPR, First Aid and Automated External Defibrillator
state_specifics: A staff member with current First Aid and CPR cards must be in the facility at all times (59A-36.010(3)(a)5; 59A-36.011(5)).

CPR certification must require in-person skills demonstration and be issued by an instructor or provider approved by the American Red Cross, American Heart Association, National Safety Council or an organization accredited by the Commission on Accreditation for Pre-Hospital Continuing Education (59A-36.011(5)(a)).
A nurse counts as having First Aid. An EMT or paramedic certified under ch. 401, part III counts for both (59A-36.010(3)(a)5.b).
Facilities with 17 or more beds must keep a working AED on the premises at all times (s. 429.255(3)(a), per research).
Staff honor a valid DH Form 1896 (59A-36.009(3)).

policies.title: Food Service and Therapeutic Diets
state_specifics: The administrator or a designee in writing is responsible for total food service and day-to-day supervision of food staff. A designee without core training must complete the core course's food and nutrition module before assuming responsibility. Exempt: certified food manager, certified dietary manager, RD/LD, dietetic registered technician, health department sanitarian (59A-36.012(1)).

The administrator or designee also needs 2 hours of annual CE in nutrition and food service (59A-36.011(7)). Staff who prepare or serve food and have not taken core training need 1 hour of safe food handling within 30 days (59A-36.011(3)(e)).
Meals follow the USDA Dietary Guidelines for Americans 2020-2025 and the Dietary Reference Intakes (2019). Standardized recipes are required except at 16 or fewer residents (59A-36.012(2)(a)-(b)).
A dietitian, nutritionist or supervised RDT reviews all regular and therapeutic menus annually, with signature, license/registration number and date. Show portion sizes (59A-36.012(2)(c)).
Menus dated and planned at least 1 week ahead, posted or easily available. Keep menus as served, with substitutions noted, for 6 months (59A-36.012(2)(d)).
Therapeutic diets as ordered by the provider. Document refusals and notify the provider (59A-36.012(2)(e)).
Maximum 14 hours from an evening protein meal to the morning meal. 2 to 6 hours between meals. Snack at least daily for residents without kitchen access (59A-36.012(2)(f)).
3-day supply of nonperishable food based on census, plus water or a reviewed water plan (59A-36.012(2)(h)).

Keep 2 years of county health department inspection reports (ch. 64E-12 or 64E-11 by capacity). Per research, DOH food hygiene inspection is required for 11+ beds. Keep contracts and contractor licenses for contracted food service (59A-36.012(3)-(4)).

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
state_specifics: Provide an ongoing activities program with diversified individual and group activities suited to each resident's needs, abilities and interests (59A-36.007(2)(a)).

Scheduled activities at least 6 days a week for at least 12 hours per week. Television does not count unless it is a special one-time event of interest to residents. Outside day program hours may be counted (59A-36.007(2)(c)).
Post an activities calendar in common areas (59A-36.007(2)(c)). Up to 3 hours may be credited when residents help plan a special activity (59A-36.007(2)(d)).

Consult residents on selecting, planning and scheduling activities, and demonstrate this by meetings, committees, a resident council, a monitored suggestion box, group discussions or questionnaires (59A-36.007(2)(b)).

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
state_specifics: Furnishings if provided by the facility: bed with mattress at least 36x72 inches, closet or wardrobe space, dresser, nightstand or table, lamp, wastebasket and a chair on request. Master keys to bedrooms are kept by the facility. Provide linens and laundry service (59A-36.014(3), per research).
House rules must state administrative and housekeeping schedules and requirements (59A-36.007(5)(d)6).
Residents may be required to clean their own sleeping areas only if the rules or contract say so (59A-36.007(5)(e)).
Maintenance changes that alter capacity or convert uninspected space to resident use need prior AHCA approval (59A-36.004(2)-(3)).
Emergency power equipment must be maintained and tested under contract (59A-36.025(1)(c)).

policies.title: Transportation
state_specifics: The facility must provide transportation to needed medical, dental, nursing or mental health services, or arrange it through family, friends, volunteers, taxis, public buses or agencies (59A-36.007(3)(b)).
Assist residents with making and remembering appointments (59A-36.007(3)(a)).
State in the admission package the availability and cost of transportation (59A-36.006(3)(a)6). Charges beyond the contract rate need an itemized notice and signed addendum (59A-36.018(3)).
Evacuation transportation is addressed in the CEMP (59A-36.019(1)(c)).
Resident-friendly independence: the resident may travel independently in the community (59A-36.007(1)(c)).

policies.title: Staffing Levels and Supervision
state_specifics: Minimum staff hours per week by combined residents, day care participants and respite residents: 0-5 = 168; 6-15 = 212; 16-25 = 253; 26-35 = 294; 36-45 = 335; 46-55 = 375; 56-65 = 416; 66-75 = 457; 76-85 = 498; 86-95 = 539; plus 42 hours for every 20 over 95 (59A-36.010(3)(a)1).
Independent living residents who receive no personal, LNS or ECC services do not count (59A-36.010(3)(a)2).

At least one staff member with access to facility and resident records must be in the facility at all times when residents are present. Residents serving as paid or volunteer staff may not be left solely in charge (59A-36.010(3)(a)3).
At 17 or more residents, at least one staff member must be awake at all hours (59A-36.010(3)(a)4).

Maintenance, grounds, clerical and food-preparation-only staff do not count toward the hours. The administrator or manager counts if actively involved in day-to-day operation and on the staffing schedule. Only on-the-job staff count (59A-36.010(3)(a)7-9).
Enough qualified staff must be on hand to meet residents' scheduled and unscheduled needs, contracts and the care standards (59A-36.010(3)(b)).

Keep a written work schedule showing the 24-hour staffing pattern. Provide direct care staff schedules to residents or representatives on request (59A-36.010(3)(c)). Keep written schedules and time sheets for the most current 6 months (59A-36.015(2)(c)).
AHCA can require staff above the minimum. The facility must provide staff immediately and submit a corrective action plan when required (59A-36.010(3)(d)).
LMH, ECC and LNS licensees must also meet 59A-36.020, .021 and .022 staffing rules (59A-36.010(3)(f)).
At 17+ licensed capacity, written job descriptions and time sheets are required (59A-36.010(2)(e)).
Pay at least $15.00/hour from Sept 30, 2026 (Fla. Const. Art. X, s. 24).

policies.title: Administrator and Manager Qualifications and Absence Coverage
state_specifics: Administrator: at least 21, a high school diploma or GED (if employed on or after 10/30/1995), Level 2 screening, core training and competency test no later than 90 days after becoming administrator, and continuing education (59A-36.010(1)(a)).

Core training: minimum 26 hours plus a competency test, with a 75% minimum passing score. Test fee may not exceed $200 per attempt. Licensed nursing home administrators are exempt. Completion within 3 months (59A-36.011(1)). An administrator who lets CE lapse must retake the core training and competency test (59A-36.011(1)(d)).
12 hours of CE related to assisted living every 2 years (59A-36.011(1)(c)). ECC and LMH CE count toward it as described in 59A-36.011(8)-(9).
Extenuating circumstances (such as the administrator's death): AHCA may allow an individual to serve temporarily for up to 90 days while completing the training (59A-36.010(1)(b)).

When the administrator or manager is absent for more than 48 hours with residents on the premises, a designated staff member at least 21 years old must be physically present and designated in writing. No staff member may be in charge for 21 or more consecutive days or 60 total days per calendar year unless an administrator or manager (59A-36.010(3)(a)6).
An administrator over more than one facility appoints a written manager for each facility (59A-36.010(1)(c)).

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: Level 2 screening applies to the administrator, managers and staff, including staff contracted by the facility to provide services to residents (59A-36.010(1)(a)3, (2)(f); ss. 408.809, 429.174).
Use the AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse (s. 435.12). Clearinghouse help line is 850-412-4503 per research.
Rescreen every 5 years (s. 408.809(2), per research).

Keep documentation of Level 2 compliance in each personnel record (59A-36.015(2)(a)3). For staff supplied by a licensed staffing agency, keep the contract rather than personnel records, and ensure the contract describes the services provided (59A-36.010(2)(d); 59A-36.015(2)(b)).
Controlling interests are also screened (per research; AHCA Form 3110-1008 and addendum 3110-1024).

This base set lists no separate nurse aide registry mandate for a standard ALF. Confirm any licensure verification through the DOH license lookup for nurses, and keep copies of licenses (59A-36.015(2)(a)2).

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
state_specifics: Preservice orientation: at least 2 hours before interacting with residents for new employees who have not completed core training. The employee and the administrator sign a statement kept in the personnel record. It must cover resident rights and the facility's license type and services (59A-36.011(2)).

Within 30 days for direct care staff: 1 hour on reporting adverse incidents and emergency procedures; 1 hour on resident rights and abuse, neglect and exploitation (if not core-trained); 3 hours on resident behavior and needs and ADL assistance (except nurses, CNAs and HHAs); HIV/AIDS one-time course (s. 381.0035) within 30 days; elopement response training for all staff (59A-36.011(3)-(4)).
1 hour of infection control before providing personal care (59A-36.011(3)(a)).
Food handlers: 1 hour of safe food handling within 30 days if not core-trained (59A-36.011(3)(e)).
Medication assistance: 6 hours with a RN or pharmacist before assuming the duty, then 2 hours annually (59A-36.011(6)).
First Aid and CPR: see SAF-10. ADRD training: see HCS-05. ECC and LMH training: see HCS-11 and HCS-12.
Staff must be qualified for their duties by education, training and experience (59A-36.010(2)(b)). Keep documentation of all required training in personnel records (59A-36.015(2)(a)1).

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: Within 30 days of hire, new staff must submit a written statement from a health care provider that the person has no signs or symptoms of communicable disease. The exam must have been done no earlier than 6 months before submission. Staff transferring without a break in service between facilities under the same ownership or management are not "new" (59A-36.010(2)(a)).

Document a negative tuberculosis examination every year. A DOH or provider statement of a TB testing material shortage satisfies the annual requirement. A positive test needs a provider statement that the person is not a risk (59A-36.010(2)(a)1).
Staff who have or are suspected of having a communicable disease are removed immediately from duties until a written provider statement shows no risk (59A-36.010(2)(a)2).
Keep the documentation in the personnel record (59A-36.015(2)(a)). Apply OSHA bloodborne pathogen requirements if applicable.
